# `silk/cli/value`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

How a struct field reads its value from the command line.

## When to use
Every field of a command struct needs [`ArgValue`](#ArgValue). This module implements it for `String`,
`bool`, the integer types, `Option<T>`, and `List<T>`. Implement it for your own type to read
that type from an argument.

## Details
A `bool` field is a flag: it takes no value and becomes `true` when the flag is present. An
`Option<T>` field becomes present when the option is given. A `List<T>` field collects every
occurrence, and as a positional argument it takes every remaining argument.

Import as `ArgValue` with `import silk.cli.value { ArgValue }`.

Public declarations: 2.

<a id="FromArg"></a>

## `FromArg`

```silk
pub interface FromArg
```

A type that reads one value from command-line text.

<a id="FromArg.fromArg"></a>

### Operation `fromArg`

```silk
effect fn fromArg(text: string) -> Result<Self, bool> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the value that `text` spells, or `false` in `Result.Failure` when `text` is not a
valid value.

<a id="ArgValue"></a>

## `ArgValue`

```silk
pub interface ArgValue
```

A field type that the parser can fill from the command line.

<a id="ArgValue.takesValue"></a>

### Operation `takesValue`

```silk
fn takesValue() -> bool
```

Whether an occurrence of the option takes a value. `false` makes the option a flag.

<a id="ArgValue.repeats"></a>

### Operation `repeats`

```silk
fn repeats() -> bool
```

Whether the field accepts more than one occurrence.

<a id="ArgValue.initial"></a>

### Operation `initial`

```silk
effect fn initial() -> Self ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the value of a field that the command line does not give: empty text, zero,
`false`, `none`, or an empty list.

<a id="ArgValue.accept"></a>

### Operation `accept`

```silk
effect fn accept(self: &mut Self, text: string) -> bool ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Stores one occurrence. `text` is empty for a flag. Returns `false` when `text` is not a valid
value.
